name: Provider descriptor registry and secret-field routing (Tenant Governance · TK-4131/TK-4132)
skipReason: A typed data registry and a pure split function — no runtime route exists. Verified by tests/platform/scopedConfig.test.ts (9 assertions), which loops EVERY descriptor rather than one example.
description: Declares each configurable provider (cloud region, object storage, email, payment, AI) as data rather than as page code, so adding a provider is adding a descriptor instead of writing another settings page — the config page previously carried this list inline, which is why each portal grew its own copy. Every field declares whether it is a SECRET, and splitSecretFields() is the single enforcement point for the rule that matters: config_value.value is plain JSONB and is returned by ordinary GET /api/config reads, so a credential written there is readable by every caller allowed to read configuration. Secrets are therefore routed to secret_ref (the sdk-secrets envelope) and never into value. The driver name deliberately STAYS in value: knowing a tenant uses SendGrid is not a credential, and requiring a vault decrypt to learn it would make every send path pay for it. The test asserts the negative for every descriptor with traceable per-field values, so a provider added later cannot silently regress the rule, and asserts the INVERSE too — Stripe publishable_key must not be secret, because vaulting it would break the browser client that has to embed it.

testCases.name: No secret-flagged field reaches config_value.value, for every descriptor
A publishable key is not treated as a secret
Every provider category has at least one descriptor
Blank fields are omitted rather than stored as empty strings

errorCases.name: A credential-shaped field left unflagged fails the suite
errorCases.when: someone adds a provider with an api_key/token/password field and forgets the secret flag; the check is on the DATA rather than on anyone remembering the convention, because the resulting leak would be silent

errorCases.name: A secret written into value would fail the suite
errorCases.when: splitSecretFields is bypassed or a page writes the raw form to /api/config; value is returned by ordinary config reads so this is a disclosure, not a style issue
